slides.title: Placement New Concept
slides.prompt: Placement new constructs an object inside a pre-allocated raw memory buffer supplied by the user. Because memory is managed separately, objects constructed with placement new must be destroyed by explicitly calling their destructor.

slides.title: Placement New Syntax
slides.prompt: Fill in the placement new syntax to construct object T inside raw memory address 'buf'.

slides.title: Destroying Placement New Objects
slides.prompt: Why must you NEVER call 'delete ptr;' on an object constructed via placement new on a custom stack buffer?
options: delete tries to free memory to the heap, causing runtime corruption when address isn't from heap new
Explicit destructors are called twice automatically
slides.correctAnswer: delete tries to free memory to the heap, causing runtime corruption when address isn't from heap new

slides.title: Explicit Destructor Invocation
slides.prompt: Fill in the syntax to explicitly invoke the destructor for pointer variable 'pObj'.

slides.title: Memory Alignment Requirement
slides.prompt: What constraint must be satisfied by raw memory passed to placement new?
options: The memory address must be properly aligned for object type T (e.g. via alignas or std::aligned_storage)
The buffer size must be exactly 1024 bytes
The memory address must be allocated using malloc
The buffer must be initialized to zero bytes
slides.correctAnswer: The memory address must be properly aligned for object type T (e.g. via alignas or std::aligned_storage)
